newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peru hostage siege has precedents in Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Peru hostage siege has precedents in Latin America.

text.p: Peru's hostage siege, which ended on Tuesday when troops stormed the Japanese embassy residence to free captive VIPs, was the most notorious but not the only such crisis in recent Latin American history.
On February 27, 1980, Colombian M-19 guerrillas stormed the Dominican Republic's embassy in Bogota, taking a total of 80 hostages, 14 of whom were ambassadors.

The guerrillas demanded the release of 209 political prisoners and a $50 million cash payment. After 61 days of negotiations and the involvement of Cuban leader Fidel Castro, the rebels were flown to Cuba where they released 13 diplomats they had taken with them.
Colombian President Julio Turbay Ayala said then that the outcome of the crisis had been "a victory for democracy".
Five years later, on November 6, 1985, the M-19 guerrillas struck again, storming Colombia's Supreme Court.

Showing little patience for negotiations, President Belisario Betancur ordered a rescue operation in which 215 hostages were released but another 115 people died, including the President of Colombia's Supreme Court.
An ensuing investigation was unable to determine if the deaths had been the result of guerrilla or armed forces fire.
Colombia is currently suffering a hostage drama after the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) overran an army base in a remote area of southwest Colombia last August 30.

At least 60 soldiers are being held hostage by the FARC guerrillas and negotiations have been stuck since December, largely because of mutual antagonisms and deep distrust between the military and the FARC's 70-year-old commander, Manuel Marulanda. Adding insult to injury, the FARC took 10 other troops hostage in January in northwestern Choco province.
Internationally, some of the most high-profile hostage dramas included the following:

- A Palestinian guerrilla group kidnapped nine Israeli athletes in the midst of the 1972 Olympic Games in Munich. A botched rescue operation by German security forces ended with the deaths of all the athletes.

- Four years later, on June 27, 1976, Palestinians kidnapped an Air France jetliner and took all 268 people on board hostage. The plane landed in Entebbe, Uganda, where the guerrillas demanded the release of Palestinian prisoners held in Israel.

On July 3, 200 Israeli soldiers landed in Entebbe and managed in 53 minutes to release all but three hostages who were killed in the fight. All guerrillas were killed as well as some 100 Ugandan military forces.

A 1985 Palestinian-led attack on the Italian liner Achille Lauro and the November 4, 1979, taking of the U.S. embassy in Tehran, Iran, with 52 hostages inside were also among the most dramatic hostage crises in recent memory.
